title: The Hero's Journey: Campbell's Universal Pattern
description: The story pattern hidden in myths, movies, and our own lives.

questions.question: Campbell claimed roughly what percentage of world mythologies follow the Hero's Journey?
questions.explanation: Campbell found recognizable monomyth elements in over 90% of mythologies he studied.

questions.question: In over 90% of myths Campbell studied, what does he call the hero's reluctance after the call?
questions.explanation: The Refusal mirrors real human resistance to change.

questions.question: After the Refusal of the Call, Campbell's Supernatural Aid figure represents what Jungian archetype?
questions.explanation: Supernatural aids project the Self—the psyche's guiding wisdom.

questions.question: Campbell's Self archetype surfaces in kings—Arthur's name derives from a word meaning what animal?
questions.explanation: Celtic 'Artos' links Arthur to Ursa Major and cyclical kingship.

questions.question: That bear-king pattern leads to crisis—what Greek word for turning point did Campbell cite?
questions.explanation: Greek 'krisis' means the moment of decision when identity must reorganize.
